articleTitle: File Access Characteristics of Deep Learning Workloads and Cache-Friendly Data Management
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Recently, the data size of deep learning grows rapidly, and accessing file data can significantly degrade deep learning performance. To quantify this, we analyze the file access characteristics of deep learning workloads and find out that they are quite different from those of traditional workloads. Specifically, in the deep learning’s training process, all file data are randomly accessed, and due to this feature, it is difficult to improve the performance of file access through caching. To cope with this situation, we present a cache-friendly file data management policy for accelerating data access in deep learning. Unlike conventional deep learning training processes that shuffle all datasets every epoch, our policy defines a shuffling unit called bundle, and improves the spatial locality of file access without compromising the model’s training efficiency. We also improve the temporal locality of data access by arranging bundles in an alternating order for each epoch. Experimental results show that our data management policy improves the miss ratio of file cache by 17.0%, and the execution time of training by 24.7% when accessing file data in deep learning.

articleTitle: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection using Autistic Image Dataset
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are neurodevelopmental disorders that are marked by enduring difficulties with speech, nonverbal communication, and restricted or repetitive behaviors. Early detection and intervention can greatly improve outcomes for people with ASD. Recently, deep learning algorithms have been applied to aid in the early detection of ASD using facial images. In this work, modifications of the commonly used VGG16 and VGG19 models for image recognition tasks are proposed to improve the performance of detecting ASD from a child’s frontal face image. The proposed model is unique, as it alters the architecture of existing models, adds an attentional mechanism, and applys transfer learning. These changes are intended to decrease the chance of overfitting and enhance the model’s capacity to capture subtle face characteristics. The performance of the updated model is assessed through accuracy, which is 82.55% for VGG19 and 80% for VGG16 model, and contrasted the outcomes of the original model. Performance of the modified model is also compared with that of the original model. The obtained results show that the modified model outperforms in detecting ASD from facial images, suggesting that the proposed modification is non-invasive for early detection of ASD and has the potential to contribute to the development of efficient tools.

articleTitle: Analysis of Channel Estimation Techniques for MIMO Wireless Channel Models
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Channel estimation is a critical component in modern wireless communication systems, as it enables reliable transmission of information over fading channels. Channel estimation methods are necessary to lessen the effects of noise, interference, and other impairments that affect transmission quality. In recent years, various channel estimation methods have been suggested to enhance the performance of wireless communication systems. However, designing an efficient channel estimation algorithm remains a challenging task due to the complexity of wireless channels and the limitations of the hardware. Channel estimation is an important task in wireless communication systems and to enhance the performance we have made use of channel equalizers. In this paper two distinct channel estimation methods are compared. For a NxN Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) system, perform Least Square Estimation (LSE), Minimum Mean Square Estimation (MMSE), and plot Mean Square Error vs Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR).In Rayleigh, Rician, and Nakagami-m fading channels, MMSE method outperforms LSE.

articleTitle: Analysis of DDoS Attacks on IoT Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The primary aim of this research is to classify Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks based on the perception, transport, and application layers of the IoT architecture, as well as their operational mechanism and execution tools. The objective is to contribute to the gaps in the previous research and provide recommendations for building effective defenses against DDoS attacks on IoT architecture. The research key conclusions include a better knowledge of DDoS attacks on IoT architecture. The research provides recognition of the gaps in earlier works and recommendation for creating powerful defenses to DDoS attack in IoT. The research discusses distinctive approach in contributing to the field of IoT security by offering a thorough examination of DDoS attacks on IoT architecture.

articleTitle: Implementation of Object Recognition Integrated with Mixed Reality
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: A laboratory is a specific room or space equipped with equipment for conducting experiments, investigations, and the like. The use of a laboratory must be based on a certain scientific method. This enables all experiments, research, testing activities, calibration, learning practices, and certain material product development to run smoothly and achieve their goals. The aim of this thesis is to develop a smart lab based on mixed reality and object recognition technology, which is useful for detecting or recognizing objects in an image based on their shape or dataset. This research uses object recognition as an approach that is expected to improve the ease of operating IoT devices to detect objects in the laboratory. The input used is the real-time view of the object. The detected object image is displayed using Hololens 2 and Magic Leap, which will show relevant information.

articleTitle: Combining conditional random fields and word embeddings to improve Amazigh part-of-speech Tagging
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Part-of-speech tagging is considered a key task in natural language processing projects. Part-of-speech taggers that use classical conditional random fields perform very well in well-studied and rich language reaching 97%. However, in low-resourced language like Amazigh language, the accuracy of the conditional random fields model with features extraction is less than 90% in tagging. In this paper, we present a new part-of-speech tagging model using conditional random fields with the integration of word-embeddings. This method uses word-embeddings as features instead of the function of extracting features that is usually used in conditional random fields models. Because the Amazigh language suffers from the absence of pretrained word-embeddings, we designed a word-embedding layer that is trained gradually as the model. We used an existing dataset of 60k tokens and a tagset of 28 tags to evaluate our model. The accuracy of our proposed model reaches 96.78 %. The result is compared with other state-of-art Amazigh part-of-speech taggers that used conditional random fields. This comparison shows that our approach outperforms the other techniques in terms of accuracy. In the future, will continue enriching the Amazigh language with more natural language processing applications and datasets.

articleTitle: Enhancing Supply Chain Management: A Blockchain-Based Approach for Data Privacy and Transparency in the IoT Era
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) has spurred the growth of smart devices, smart buildings and smart cities worldwide. Supply chain management is a cross functional approach where the various stakeholders are involved, and movement of raw and finished materials and manufacturing process happens. In supply chain Management, the customer or the manufacturers have to trust on the internal or the external stakeholders for continued operation. Blockchain came into existence to provide traceability and visibility of the process in the supply chain management. Thus, in this paper, with the integration of IoT and supply chain management, the proposed model introduces a novel and unique methodology that leverages blockchain technology to address data privacy concerns among stakeholders. The methodology involves the creation of a blockchain within a blockchain, which ensures the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive information, such as manufacturing costs, while maintaining the overall transparency and traceability of the supply chain process.

articleTitle: CNN-BiLSTM for Power Consumption Prediction using Raspberry Pi 4
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Power consumption prediction has an important role in efficient energy management, enabling better utilization of resources and cost savings. Conventional methods have often faced challenges in accurately predicting power consumption due to the complexities inherent in real-world energy systems. In order to tackle the problem, an approach utilizing a CNN-BiLSTM model in combination with Raspberry Pi 4, Arduino Uno R3, and PZEM 004T is presented. In this study, a seven-day experiment is conducted to implement the CNN-BiLSTM model for power consumption prediction. The model is trained on the collected data and subsequently tested on unseen samples. The results obtained demonstrate the effectiveness of the CNN-BiLSTM model, with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 3.0906, which indicates low prediction errors.

articleTitle: Masked Face Recognition and Identification Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, everyone has been instructed to wear a face mask that blocks the lower part of their facial area. Only a few existing face recognition models are able to detect and recognize masked faces yet, the average accuracy has worsened when compared to the ones that detect an entire face of a person. Therefore, the objective of this study is to develop new models capable of detecting and recognizing masked faces, and compare their performance with existing models. Three convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are used, namely VGG16, VGGFace, and InceptionResNetV2 (IRv2). Many experimental cases are considered including the cases where only masked-face images are used, or the other two cases where both full-face and masked-face images are used together. The models give maximum accuracy at 93.3% where 50 individuals are recognized and identified.

articleTitle: Design of An Electrical Regenerative Braking System for E-Bike Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Electric bikes (e-bikes) are emerging as a cleaner, more efficient, and more comfortable transportation solution. However, challenges like limited range and battery recharging accessibility persist. A potential solution is a regenerative braking system, converting braking kinetic energy into electric energy stored in the battery. This study introduces an e-bike tailored with an electrical regenerative braking system. It provides assembly details and evaluates three aspects: regenerative mode, battery mode, and regenerative braking performance. Results confirm the e-bike’s successful operation. The regenerative mode’s voltage and current align with battery specs. Energy consumption increase matches battery mode mileage. In final testing, reverse voltage and current from regenerative braking meet battery specs. Despite slight differences, the average voltage among the three speeds does not significantly contrast with the average current. As speed rises, the average current follows. This underscores regenerative braking’s compliance with specifications and its non-harmful impact on the battery’s lifespan.

articleTitle: Internet-Based Control System of Things on Cylinder Regulator for Safety from LPG Gas Leak Hazards
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Consumption of using LPG cylinders has become a major human need for daily needs. But behind its use, there are dangers that can occur at any time when using LPG cylinders. Lack of concern for maintaining and monitoring LPG cylinder installations can have a large impact on losses. To detect LPG gas leaks, researchers used the MQ-6 sensor and the Arduino Uno microcontroller. The MQ-6 sensor is an input device that can receive data in the form of LPG gas levels. While Arduino Uno is a processing tool that receives data from sensors to be processed and outputs results in the form of information on detected gas leak levels and follow-up actions in the form of a rotating regulator valve and detached from the LPG gas cylinder. This action applies automatically if the detected gas level is more than 5 ppm. There is also an Android-based application that displays real-time detected gas levels, as well as an action button to rotate the regulator valve.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Monolith, Microservice API Gateway and Microservice Federated Gateway on Web-based application using GraphQL API
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to provide a detailed explanation regarding the characteristics as well as the pros and cons offered by various software development architecture, such as monolithic and Microservice architecture implemented with graph-based API called GraphQL. Monolithic architecture offers a centralized software development pattern with relatively simpler integration and development process. Conversely, Microservices architecture such as Gateway Aggregation and Federated Gateway will divide independent components of the application into smaller modules. Gateway Aggregation utilizes a single Gateway which acts as the main entry point for data exchange between the client and the application. In this research aims an application is developed using the three different architectures to measure the quality, both qualitative and quantitative performances of each architecture. There are several different parameters that are going to be used to measure the architecture’s performance such as response time and data throughput which become an essential criterion in conducting load and stress testing. The result is that the Monolithic architecture offers some advantages in its quantitative performance measurement due to better efficiency in collecting and processing requested data in a single application which utilizes fewer resources and shorter time. In contrast, the Gateway Aggregation architecture and Federated Gateway architecture also have some significant performance differences because it costs resources to combine several subgraphs together into a valid graph.

articleTitle: Digital Forensics for Ancient Manuscripts Using Local Thickness and Independent Component Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Degeneration and destruction of the ancient manuscripts have sustained through time presenting serious problems for their preservation and interpretation. Nevertheless, it contains important to be restored, authenticated, and studied using digital image forensics, a specialist area of image analysis. This study aims to identify to explore the possibility of patterns or detailed information that cannot be observed by the naked eye in these ancient manuscripts. In this study, it applicates ancient Indonesian manuscripts from different periods. To analyse it, we apply an analytical method with Local Thickness and Independent Component Analysis (ICA) approaches. In the ICA experiment, no significant details or information were found. However, in the local thickness analysis, there were differences in local thickness between two manuscripts from different periods. The value of this work is to enhance knowledge about digital imaging in ancient manuscripts.

articleTitle: Hysteresis Amplifier Model to Eliminate Multi-switching on IGBT Work
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The occurrence of multi-switching on an isolated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) function can cause significant power dissipation and disrupt the power network. To overcome this problem, this paper designs a hysteresis amplifier model to reduce multi-switching in IGBTs. This software is used to simulate and analyze the performance of the hysteresis model amplifier. The hysteresis amplifier design is used to induce a hysteresis effect on the IGBT control signal. This effect produces an output frequency of 50 Hz with a 50% duty cycle. The working mechanism of this design includes the formation of a hysteresis window on the IGBT control signal, +2.00 V to +2.52 V. If the design result of the control signal is at least +2.50 V to +2.48 V, the IGBT enters the active state when Vout1 reaches +3.51 V. The design results in the control signal reaching a maximum value of +2.50 V to +2.51 V. The IGBT transitions to the active state when the voltage at Vout2 reaches a threshold of +3.51 V. The automatic implementation of the hysteresis window effectively reduces the occurrence of multi-switching by ensuring that a switch event occurs when the control signal is within the specified hysteresis window range. The current transformer detects changes in current through the variable resistor when Vin +2.00V to Vin +2.52 V. By understanding the characteristics and implementation of the model, it is possible to formulate intelligent control strategies aimed at increasing the efficiency and stability of system power through the use of IGBT.

articleTitle: Classification of Text on Social Media Data Using the TF-IDF Approach, Word2Vec and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: On social media, there is a lot of information that can be used for further analysis, such as text data, including posts, comments, and reviews. The data has unstructured properties. The problem in this study is the difficulty of analyzing text on social media data to determine standard and non-standard words, so this research utilizes an approach from word representation with TF-IDF, Word2Vec, and transfer learning and using the CNN algorithm. This study produced 3 models in classification performance. In the evaluation model 3 obtained better accuracy compared to model 1 and model 2 because the number of epochs and batch sizes were different. For model 3, the accuracy obtained based on batch values of 64 and epoch values of 20 is 82% for the TF-IDF-CNN model, while the second model uses Word2Vec-CNN with batch values of 128 and epoch values of 60 to obtain 86% accuracy for the Transfer Learning-CNN model with batch values of 256 and epoch values of 100, the accuracy obtained is 91%.

articleTitle: A Novel Signal-to-Image Conversion Approach with Ensembles of Pretrained CNNs for Motor Imagery EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Deep learning techniques can recognize and learn significant features automatically. The advantages of deep learning should also be used to solve problems in other fields. Therefore, we concentrated on classifying motor imagery EEG signals with deep transfer learning. The present study first proposed an EEG signal-to-image conversion method that uses 2D signal representations. Thanks to this, we employed 2D images as input instead of standard one-dimensional EEG features. Second, we used AlexNet, GoogLeNet, and SqueezeNet pre-trained convolutional neural network frameworks for classification. We also used hard voting and merged the outputs of pre-trained convolutional neural networks. We performed experiments on dataset 2a of BCI Competition IV, achieving 84.18±5.37% classification accuracy and 0.66±0.12 kappa across nine subjects, even with limited training data. The results showed that the proposed signal-to-image conversion method with deep transfer learning has potential, particularly in processing biomedical signals.

articleTitle: Comparative Phishing Attack Simulations: A Case Study of Critical Information Infrastructure Organization Using Two Different Contents
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Nowadays, cybersecurity is an important issue at the personal and organizational levels. Therefore, cybersecurity simulation should be conducted in organizations that are considered critical information infrastructure. According to the simulated phishing attack, during the initial attempt, an email offering a fake promotion from a well-known IT equipment store was sent to employees of a railway company in Thailand. The results indicated that out of around 700 employees who received these phishing emails, 9.5% fell for the trap. This demonstrated a higher level of awareness about cyber threats compared to the average rate of 12%. However, the training was performed for the employees who fell into the trap of the first attack. Then, a simulated phishing email attack was executed for the second time by sending an email, notifying the employees to change their passwords, from a fake IT administrator. The results revealed that 8.0% of the employees who do not fall in the first attack were deceived, while there was 1.4% of the employees who fell into both attacks with different contents. Therefore, this study shows that different contents can impact different awareness of users or employees. Thus, it suggests that the process of knowledge transfer based on cybersecurity awareness is very important still.

articleTitle: Hybrid Model for Topic Classification of English Learning Accounts on Instagram Using LDA and SVM
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: English is an important international language to master, especially when in places with different language speakers. However, according to the EF English Proficiency Index, English proficiency among Indonesians is still very low. Indonesia ranks 74 out of 100 countries. Nowadays, many people use social media platforms, like Instagram, to share information and learn. There are numerous English learning accounts on Instagram with thousands of posts, making it difficult to group the topics found in these posts. Therefore, topic modeling and classification need to be performed to determine which topics account owners should improve to attract learners' interest. In this paper, the authors used the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) method for topic modeling and Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classification. The authors also compared the results when the labeling was done by experts. The expert labeling resulted in 9 topics, while using LDA produced 6 topics. This indicates that the topics generated by the experts are more specific compared to LDA. However, the SVM classification accuracy results from the LDA model are higher compared to the manual labeling. Specifically, the SVM classification accuracy using the polynomial kernel is 79.33%, using the sigmoid kernel is 79.33%, and using the RBF kernel is 80.00% for the LDA model. On the other hand, the SVM classification accuracy using the polynomial kernel is 35.33%, using the sigmoid kernel is 33.67%, and using the RBF kernel is 33.67% for the manual labeling.

articleTitle: Utilizing Clustering Algorithms to Provide Vark Learning Style Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The term "learning style" refers to the approach preferred by individuals to acquiring knowledge. Fleming and Mills introduced an interesting method called VARK (Visual, Audio, Read/Write, Kinesthetic) to observe learning styles. VARK has been widely used in numerous studies to understand how students prefer to receive information. This research aims to identify clusters of student learning styles in order to enhance the quality of education. E-learning enables students to learn in a manner similar to traditional classrooms, even without the presence of teachers or educators. The study collected data from 138 students attending 16 meetings on campus. Based on the findings and discussions, the following conclusions can be drawn: the Split Validation accuracy test indicates that the K-Means algorithm has a Davies-Bouldin Index (DBI) value of 0.475, the X-Means algorithm has a DBI value of 0.478, and the K-Medoids algorithm has a DBI value of 0.699. The K-Means algorithm yields the best result, with a DBI value of 0.475, which is considered good as it is the smallest value obtained. A smaller DBI value or a value closer to zero indicates a more accurate cluster. Based on the visual results, students predominantly exhibit a preference for the VISUAL and AUDIO learning styles, as recommended by the K-Means algorithm.

articleTitle: Mobile Application Malware Self-Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Daily wise, people used various mobile applications, where those applications offer social communication, online shopping, gaming, and other services. However, the rapid spread of mobile applications increases the cyber-attacks surface exponentially, since there are millions of applications that have threats and can exploit user's poor knowledge of security, which leads to difficulties to protect the user from all threats by depending only on traditional methods. Based on that we start to develop an automated system that can protect mobile users without human intervention. The system was developed using the Case-Based Reasoning technique. We proposed a method that can solve a new security issue in mobile applications based on historical solutions stored on the case base has common similarities. For any security issue, some features or attributes can be used to be matched with historically solved security issues. The system selects the appropriate solution based on the nearest similar case from the case base. And the system stores the newly solved case in the case base to achieve self-learning.

articleTitle: Intelligent IoT-based Combined Crop-type and Disease Prediction System with Different Machine Learning & Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Agriculture contributes significantly to economic and social prosperity around the world. The world's population is increasing rapidly, so the food demand is also growing. Farmers must use harmful pesticides more frequently and intensively on the soil to meet the increased demand since more than previous methods are required. Also, this strategy can occasionally result in agricultural disaster, resulting in a considerable waste of crops, money, and effort. New automated edge intelligence technology sparks a farming revolution to meet that need. An intelligent IoT-based application is a comprehensive solution that predicts crop yields and detects illness in crops by utilizing machine learning and deep learning techniques with the most popular fashionable algorithms. To create a system, we use edge intelligence. This research focuses on integrating Raspberry Pi, sensor, and Azure IoT Hub. We successfully prevented crop waste by training 2000+ data points with a 94.18% accuracy rate. In contrast, this system is automated and software-based since it is lightweight, the costs are low, and the study reacts significantly better than other existing studies.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Piezoelectric-Based Energy Harvesting in Shoes
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Energy harvesting is a method that captures energy from the environment and converts it into electrical energy. Piezoelectric energy harvesters employ external forces on piezoelectric elements to generate power. The Piezoelectric-Based Energy Harvesting system is employed to measure the power output of the piezoelectric device. This system utilizes a Wemos D1 Mini microcontroller with an integrated ESP8266 Wi-Fi module to transmit sensor data to a ubidots database. The INA219 sensors are used to measure the voltage, current, and power output of the piezoelectric device. It measures the energy harvesting performance in different conditions: walking, jogging, and running with two configuration rectifier capacitor and LTC3588. The results demonstrate that the running condition produces the highest power output. with of 2.71 mW for body weight 55 in rectifier capacitor configuration and 1,30 mW for a body weight of 55 kg in LTC3588 configuration. Furthermore, when the testing with same step, the running condition used rectifier capacitor configuration exhibits the highest output, measuring 2,73 mW for a weight of 55 kg and 1,83 mW for a weight of 55 kg in LTC3588 configuration. The output is influenced by the applied pressure on the piezoelectric device and the user's weight. These findings indicate that the output of the piezoelectric device is influenced by the applied pressure and the user's weight.

articleTitle: Sensor Fusion with Seven Parameters for Indoor Air Quality Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Indoor Air Quality is needed to be detected and monitored. Poor indoor air quality from air pollution is a global environmental concern that significantly impacts human health and ecosystems. Air pollutants can be consist of some gases, such carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, ammonia, total volatile organic compounds, and nitrogen dioxide. Indoor air quality is also related to the temperature and humidity. Therefore, monitoring air quality accurately and comprehensively is crucial for effective mitigation and policy-making. Air quality sensor fusion, a process of integrating data from multiple sensors, has emerged as an approach to enhance the accuracy and reliability of air quality monitoring systems. Combining data from diverse sensors, sensor fusion enables a more comprehensive of air pollution dynamics. Therefore, in this research, seven parameters are chosen such as Particulate Matter, Volatile Organic Compounds, Carbon Monoxide, Nitrogen Dioxides, Sulfur Dioxide, Ammonia, Temperature, and Humidity sensors are integrated to monitor indoor air quality using ESP32-WROOM-32 as a microcontroller with Arduino IDE as a platform for programming and displaying the result. The result of this research is those seven parameters can be detected and monitored on a serial monitor Arduino IDE with all calibrated sensors with compact size of the PCB design with the dimension of 100 mm × 100 mm. The development of this sensor fusion for further research can be connected to Internet of Things.

articleTitle: Control Strategy for BESS-Fed Inverters in AC Microgrids with SoC Consideration
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This paper presents a control strategy for an inverter in a battery energy storage system (BESS) within an AC microgrid, focusing on state of charge (SoC) management. The proposed control strategy employs a droop control method to regulate the active and reactive power exchanged between the inverter and the grid, considering the SoC of the BESS. The effectiveness of the control strategy is verified through a simulation using a modified CIGRE microgrid benchmark in Matlab®/ Simulink. Various case studies are performed to examine the system's ability to track reference output power values. The simulated case studies show the correlation between the SoC and the delivered output power of the inverters. The findings demonstrate that the control strategy not only balances the SoC of multiple BESS but also plays a crucial role in prolonging the battery life by operating within safe operating points of SoC. This, in turn, contributes to maintaining grid stability and effectively managing the SoC of the BESSs.

articleTitle: A Comparative Case Study of Smart and Green Buildings and Their Impact on Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The need for buildings with the concept of green building is now very important for environmental conservation. The smart building concept is to do efficiency to get better governance in optimizing a building. However, the combination of green and smart buildings is still very rare. We researched a new building belonging to the government of the Republic of Indonesia with a green building concept. With the application of smart building technology, one way is to use the latest and most modern HVAC systems. Technology by utilizing this inverter provides significant electrical efficiency. Researchers feel interested in investigating the air conditioning system used in this new building. In this research, an infestation of the quality of electrical energy was carried out due to the use of an inverter. The study results show that the harmonics of the total distortion current reach more than 5 % at a load current exceeding 159.06 amperes. In comparison, the total distortion voltage harmonics reach up to 41.83 %. The impact of this condition greatly affects the performance of the transformer. To overcome this problem, recommended using a harmonic filter on the capacitor bank.

articleTitle: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle for Remote Sensing Detection of Oil Palm Trees Using You Only Look Once and Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Oil palm (Elaeis Guineensis Jacq) is one of several palm species that produces oil for commercial purposes. Indonesia is the largest producer of palm oil in the world, thanks to its extensive plantations. The marketing of palm oil and palm kernel in Indonesia has great potential both domestically and internationally. However, the management of oil palm plantations, including the counting of palm trees, poses challenges due to the vastness of the plantations. Conventional methods of counting palm trees from aerial imagery are time-consuming and require significant additional costs. This research aims to address these issues and contribute to modern agriculture or precision farming. The dataset used consists of 500 unmanned aerial vehicle remote sensing images of oil palm trees, with an 80% training data split, 10% testing data, and 10% validation data. The algorithm used is You Only Look Once Version 7 with a convolutional neural network architecture. Testing was performed on 50 testing data of oil palm trees. The results of this study indicate that the model's performance in detecting oil palm trees achieved a precision rate of 98.45%, recall rate of 98.17%, overall accuracy of 98.31%, and a mean average precision of 99.7%.

articleTitle: Effect of TF-IDF Extraction and Application of SMOTE on Model Performance in Detecting Spam Email
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Email is one of the communication media that sends digital letters electronically using the internet. Email abuse frequently occurs, and one example of email abuse is email spam. There are many approaches that can be used to help filter email spam, but crucial techniques in text classification, such as email spam classification, include text feature extraction, as well as dataset balancing techniques like SMOTE, which can improve model performance. This research has the purpose to determine the extent of the influence of TF-IDF text feature extraction and SMOTE implementation on the performance results of the classification model. The models to be used are Naïve Bayes, Deep Learning, and K-Nearest Neighbors. Based on the results of the conducted testing, the utilization of TF-IDF and SMOTE techniques had a significant impact on the classification model, particularly on the Deep Learning model, where the accuracy increased by 44.14% and the f1 score improved by 73.75%.

articleTitle: Development of Application for Conformance Measurement of Control Affordance Components with Functional Requirements based on Text Analysis on TESA Documentation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: In application development, achieving synergy between evolving software and elicitation process outcomes emerges as a foundational objective. This endeavor is empowered by the role of text analysis, a tool that adeptly uncovers intricate data relationships and contextual intricacies. This is especially pertinent given the textual attributes of System Requirements Specification (SRS) information. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) adds depth to comprehension by converting images into text. However, challenges surface due to variances between functional requirements and the design's control and affordance components, arising from divergent interpretations of functional requirements during elicitation. Our focal point resides in crafting an application to evaluate the alignment between UI design and the textual core of functional requirements. This study reveals 13 Functional Requirements (d1-d13) and categorizes two control/affordance component documents (d14-d15). The integration of text analysis, steered by word2vec, drives an alignment process, culminating in a notable 0.397 score. Recommendations pivot on the Cohen's Kappa index; values below 0.21 prompt adjustments for alignment at a "sufficient" level (0.21 or higher). The culmination of research materializes in an advanced application adept at processing txt files, skillfully extracting inputs via text analysis, and semantically evaluating alignment through Word2Vec. It offers insights for data instances where standards fall short, firmly rooted in Cohen's Kappa index principles. This application functions as a comprehensive repository, methodically outlining enhancement suggestions, assessed against the backdrop of Cohen's Kappa index.

articleTitle: Efficiency Enhancement of The PV System Through Reconfiguration Strategies Under Non-Uniform Irradiance Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) arrays experience a significant surge in power losses due to Partially Shaded Conditions (PSCs). The presence of clouds, shadows from tall structures, trees, chimneys, and bird droppings can lead to these PSCs. When PV modules are shaded, they go into reverse bias, causing small hotspots to form and increase the system's overall temperature. To mitigate this issue, bypass diodes can be connected antiparallel to the PV modules, although this leads to multiple peaks in the I-V and P-V characteristics. Along with the challenges presented by hotspots, mismatch losses between different modules further, reduce the electricity output of a PV array. The research in focus is designed to evaluate, model, simulate, and analyze the effectiveness of several 4x4 PV array configurations operating under diverse PSCs. Topologies such as series-parallel, bridge-link, honeycomb, and total cross-tied (TCT) are investigated, along with different partial shading patterns like corners, centers, ends, L-shapes, frames, random, and diagonals. These investigations are grounded on the technical specifications of a 130-watt PV module.

articleTitle: Classification of Ischemic, Infectious, and Normal Diabetic Foot Ulcers Based on the EfficientNet Model
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic health condition that affects the way the body converts food into energy. One of the most common complications for patients with diabetes is diabetic foot ulcers (DFU). DFUs are usually located in the lower part of the leg. In general, DFU, if not treated early, will be costly and can lead to foot amputations, and death rates can increase. The study offers classification of ischemia, infection, and normality and prediction of diabetic foot ulcers with a deep learning approach. The proposed methodology uses a deep convolutional neural network model that includes four stages: preprocess augmentation, model training, validation, and classification of ischemia, infection, and normal. The model used is EfficientNet. The model that has been trained on the computer is then converted into a lite classification model. Convert and optimize models using TF Lite. The resulting model will be smaller and more optimal, so it can be used in mobile applications with the help of the TF Lite Interpreter. Android apps on mobile devices that have made the accuracy level reach 0.88, the precision value is 0.96, the recall is 1.00, and the F1 score is 0.97.

articleTitle: Optimized Kalman Filter using Genetic Algorithm for IoT Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Accurate sensor readings have an important role in ensuring the reliability of data for IoT devices. However, sensor measurements are susceptible to noise, leading to unreliable data. This research paper addresses the issue of sensor reading errors and proposes a solution using Kalman Filter to mitigate the impact of noise. The study focuses on implementing the widely known Kalman Filter, a filtering method, that can be used to reduce the influence of noise on sensor readings. Moreover, for optimizing the parameters of Kalman Filter, Genetic Algorithm is employed. The optimized parameters, denoted as Q = 9.9 and R = 0.1, represent the covariance matrices for process and measurement noise, respectively. In order to demonstrate practicality, this research utilizes the ESP32 and Analog-to-Digital Converter for collecting sensor data. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The optimized Kalman Filter can reduce the MSE caused by noise to 74.102. It indicates a noteworthy enhancement in sensor reading accuracy. This achievement holds potential for IoT applications where reliable and precise sensor data is of utmost importance. It can be concluded that by combining the Kalman Filter, Genetic Algorithm, this study contributes to the development of robust noise reduction mechanisms in IoT systems. The findings of this research offer promising prospects for enhancing the overall quality of sensor data in many IoT applications.

articleTitle: Design of a Skin Cancer Detection Classification with Python GUI and Tensorflow
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Skin cancer, which is generally classified into Melanoma Skin Cancer (MSC) and Non-Melanoma Skin Cancer (NMSC) namely Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) and Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC), is one of the most common types of cancer in humans. In this research, an application based on Python GUI and TensorFlow, known as "Early Detection Skin Cancer", is designed to detect and classify skin cancer. This application uses the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) classification method to analyse and identify skin lesions that have the potential to become cancerous. CNN is then used to identify whether the lesion is a type of SCC, BCC, or MSC. The test was carried out using validation image data from skin cancer patients at Hasan Sadikin Hospital, Bandung, with a total of 26 image data samples. The test results show that this application is capable of classifying skin cancer with 100% accuracy for MEL, 55.56% for BCC, and 42.86% for SCC. However, the quality of the images of the lesions taken can affect the classification results.

articleTitle: Perception of Privacy Concerns in Using Instagram Among Students (Case Study: Sriwijaya State Polytechnic)
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This study aims to investigate 3 things which include how the level of awareness and control regarding data privacy affects privacy concerns, how privacy concerns shape trust and risk, and investigate whether there is an influence of trust on risks arising from the use of Instagram among Informatics Management students at the State Polytechnic Sriwijaya. The data used in this research is collected from a questionnaire survey and analyzed using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM). The number of respondents was 301 obtained from the calculation of the Slovin formula. The results of the study show that there is a positive correlation between the level of awareness and control over user perceptions regarding privacy concerns and so do privacy concerns that affect the level of user trust and affect the risks that can occur from using Instagram. It's different from the perception of trust which has no influence on the perceived risk of users in using Instagram.

articleTitle: Evaluating Sign Error Correction for Approximate Adders Employing ECG Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Throughout the past decade, researchers have been captivated by approximate computing as a promising strategy that achieves both power reduction and performance enhancement. Particularly, within signal processing applications, approximate additions have received considerable attention due to their fundamental role. Regrettably, occasional sign calculation errors can lead to unexpected outcomes in certain applications. To address this concern, we have proposed an error correction technique. This paper assesses the efficacy of the suggested technique when applied to the Carry-Maskable Adder (CMA) in the context of electrocardiogram (ECG) signal processing. The findings obtained from our experiments indicate that the proposed technique enhances calculation accuracy and achieves more efficient power reduction compared to the CMA without any error correction techniques.

articleTitle: External Lightning Protection System modeling on photovoltaic using ATP Draw
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Solar energy is environmentally friendly energy with a very large energy source. Indonesia is also exploring and implementing renewable energy options including solar panels as a viable and long-term alternative to green technology. On the other hand, to get sufficient solar radiation, solar panel systems are generally located in open areas such as hillsides, deserts, and water surfaces, making them more vulnerable to lightning strikes. Lightning is one of the main threats to PLTS, a lot of damage to solar panels is caused by lightning. Direct and indirect lightning strikes have great potential to affect the entire solar panel farm system. The main objective of this study is to evaluate Lightning Protection System (LPS) modeling for network-connected solar panel (PV) farm systems using the ATP-EMTP software. Field observations and simulation tests are used to determine the position of the LPS and its installation structure. The rolling ball method is used to see the installed LPS protection radius. The results show that it is necessary to add LPS to the PV field. It was found that there was one additional LPS needed on the north side of the PV field, because that position was not protected by the radius of the lightning rod. From the simulation results, it was found that the LPS installation structure was good, because the results from the modeling of the isolated LPS lightning protection system were better to use than without installing LPS.

articleTitle: Validity of Cosine Similarity Measurement of Functional Requirements and Steps Performed Using Cohen Kappa on SRS Scenery Artifacts
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The Scenery application is informative and educative regarding tourist places in Indonesia. Differences in implementation in application development can cause a discrepancy between the client's needs that the software developer has made. Therefore, to measure success in developing the Scenery application, it is necessary to adjust and change the artifacts that form the basis of the SRS documentation. In this study, the artifact was part of the Requirements Specification in the form of Functional Requirements and part of the Use Case Description in the Step Performed. Through a Textual Similarity approach, the two artifacts were used as measuring tools to see the results of the Similarity of a software requirement between the Client and the Developer. This research uses the Cosine Similarity formula to implement Textual Similarity in Functional Requirements and Step Performed. There are results to help the functional needs of artifacts as much as 14 with document labeling from d1-d14 and for steps carried out as many as 14 with labeling from d15-d28. This study produced a matching value of -0.0290, meaning "less than chance agreement." This validity measurement can be used as a reference for improving the quality of artifacts in SRS.

articleTitle: The Effect of Augmentation on Classification Algorithm to Determine Photo Angle
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: A technique for recognizing the angle in the suitable photo is required to ensure that the information is sent correctly. The image classification method is one approach for determining the angle of a photograph. Support Vector Machine (SVM) and K-Nearest Neighbour (K-NN) classification algorithms were employed in this study. The first total dataset collected from photographic websites contained 2,700 records and was split into three classes: high angle, eye level, and low angle. In addition, there is a second dataset with 679 datasets that was also directly downloaded from the same website. This dataset is separated into 5 classes: bird's-eye view, high angle, eye level, low angle, and frog's-eye view. An augmentation method is used with three strategies, including random rotation, random noise, and grayscale, to increase the number of datasets that have been collected. The entire dataset that will be classified contains 5700 data for the first dataset and 3179 data for the second dataset after the augmentation method adds data from the first and second datasets, totaling 3000 and 2500 data, respectively. The dataset is then divided into training and testing data using a ratio of 80:20. We used 2 scenarios in developing the model: the model with additional augmented data and the model with original data. The Support Vector Machine algorithm and the K-Nearest Neighbor technique in the 3-class and 5-class classification models provide low accuracy results, particularly in the range of 50%, for testing the first scenario. In the second scenario test, the KNN technique with K = 1 achieved an accuracy of 95.10% and an execution time of 3 seconds with a number of classes of 3, compared to 91.70% and 7 seconds with a number of classes of 5. In the SVM method, the RBF kernel was able to achieve an accuracy of 94.10% with an execution time of 6 minutes 32 seconds for the number of classes 3, while 90.60% with an execution time of 26 minutes was achieved for the number of classes 5 using the same parameters (C = 10, gamma = 0.001, and RBF kernel).

articleTitle: Expert System for Screening of Borderline Personality Disorder
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Individuals who have symptoms of borderline personality disorder (BPD) usually experience intense feelings of hatred, anger, depression, or anxiety. These feelings are often frightening, overwhelming and difficult to control. In the midst of intense emotions, individuals with BPD may act impulsively to reduce emotional pain, calm themselves, or communicate emotional distress. This results in 10% of people with BPD dying by suicide. The system is made to anticipate and minimize these problems. The expert system built in this study can measure a person's level of borderline personality disorder, so that it can increase knowledge in the general public to help someone who is detected as having mental health problems or BPD. The certainty factor method is used to assume the degree of confidence in the value used, and Forward chaining as forward tracking which starts from gathering facts and events that support the assumption/hypothesis, until a conclusion is obtained. Based on tests using 50 test data using accuracy testing, it shows that the CF method has a presentation of 100% accuracy in the test results that have been carried out in this study.

articleTitle: Optimization of Feature Selection to Improve Order Transaction Performance in the Manufacturing Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The development of business processes that occur in Industry 4.0 requires the optimization of processes in the system, especially in the process of order transactions. To optimize the transaction process, the assistance of the rank and weight system on dataset features, called the feature selection process, can be employed. Feature selection aims to improve the elimination of redundant and irrelevant features, which can reduce computation time and improve accuracy. In this research using multivariate datasets. Feature selection is used to eliminate some attributes that are irrelevant to the label class, resulting in improved performance of the classification algorithm. The author compares three algorithms: information gain, ratio gain, and chi-square. These are algorithms to find the rank and weight of data. In this research to measure feature selection performance using the Naïve Bayes classifier algorithm. The evaluation is performed by observing the level of classification accuracy generated without feature selection versus the classification accuracy generated after the implementation of feature selection. The experimental results showed that 14 features were included in the selection of features, and four relevant and best features were produced using the Chi-square binary classification algorithm. Classification using naïve Bayes algorithm reached 97.56%, while using ratio gain and information gain resulted in classification values of 75.57% and 92.69%, respectively.

articleTitle: Spatial-Based 2D Image Steganography using Josephus-Traversing Concentric Midpoint Circle Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Steganography is the science of hiding secret messages within media like images and further studies have been conducted to enhance existing techniques to secure communication between parties. There are concluded studies that focus on the enhancement of individual steganography techniques like LSB, MSB, and PVD but still embed secret data in sequential order. In this kind of approach, attackers may first opt to analyze pixels in this common approach and can easily extract the hidden message. The proposed method uses Midpoint Circle Algorithm to determine the intermediate pixel locations to be used for embedding and to arrange them based on the number of skips through the concept of Josephus Problem to add confusion. The proposed method still uses the traditional LSB, MSB, and PVD approaches but image quality and security are ensured. In testing the proposed method, PSNR, MSE, and SSIM were determined, as well as the histogram and pixel differences. As a result, using these metrics, the proposed method is on par with the traditional method in terms of the quality. But since it has a new approach in embedding secret data, security is its main advantage. The recommendations for the improvement of this study include the code optimization of midpoint circle algorithm to analyze images regardless of their sizes, and for better quality and security, the acceptance of colored images and enhancement of the said spatial-based steganography techniques applied to this proposed method.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis in social media: Handling Noisy Data and Detecting Sarcasm Using a Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Social media is a platform that is highly developed with the features offered so that the use of deep learning will in the process have an artificial neural network architecture in completing tasks in certain cases. Sentiment analysis will do positive, negative and neutral assistance. The problem in this study is that the data contains in the form of slang sentences, slang and writing errors contained in social media data so that literary dictionaries and manual annotations will be applied later. can handle noisy data and can do sarcasm detection. The results obtained in this study by approaching the deep learning model with the LSTM algorithm in sentiment analysis yielded an accuracy of 0.92, a precision value of 0.83, a recall value of 0.76 and an F1 value of 0.78 while the model from RNN in detecting sarcasm has a value 0.94, precision value 0.77, recall value 0.80 and F1 value 0.85.

articleTitle: Automated Fruit Maturity Classification System for Guava (Psidium Guajava) Using K-NN Method and TCS3200 Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Guava is a climacteric fruit with short shelf life. Hence, to distribute them to consumers properly, the guava fruits need to be sorted by maturity level. The sortation process is usually done manually, lacking labor intensive, and is prone to human error. This research aims to build an automatic and accurate system that can help sort the process of Guava fruits based on the maturity level of the fruits. A K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm classification method will be implemented to classify the fruits. The features used for the classification are RGB color values extracted using the TCS3200 color sensor. The sortation system built in this research classifies the guava into three maturity levels: unripe, ripe, and overripe. For training and testing purposes, each maturity level uses ten samples of guava for training and five samples for testing. The test results obtained by varying the value of k obtained the best results, reaching 100% using k = 3 and k = 5, while k = 1, k = 7, and k = 9 obtained a percentage of 93.33%.

articleTitle: Design of Control and Data Acquisition for Smart Home Based on Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The newest technology, the Internet of Things (IoT), has a remarkable impact on raising living standards and advancing the global economy. Smart homes are one of the applications of IoT, which is also recognized in the community as a technology to facilitate global connectivity in numerous sectors. A "smart home" is a novel method of controlling home appliances like a lamp, Air Conditioner (AC), heater, and gate remotely over the internet using a Human Machine Interface (HMI). In this study, a smartphone-based prototype control and data collecting system for a smart home is presented. The major components of the system are ATMega2560 and ESP8266 microcontrollers, and the HMI system is created using Android. The system is built on Android and can measure physical amounts (metering), signaling alarm systems (signaling), and remotely operating household appliances (controlling) with ease and efficiency. The microcontroller uses an 889-millisecond interval for sending and reading data to the server. Internet connectivity and server data traffic have an impact on the success rate and communication speed. The data from the metering system accurately reflects the real-world circumstances of the prototype smart home. When applied, controlling, and signaling systems may perform well.

articleTitle: A Simple Battery Management System for Solar Powered Triangle Communication Tower
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Telecommunication towers provide reliable communication services, facilitate economic growth, and enhance social development. However, remote, isolated, and underdeveloped areas often need help establishing and maintaining a power supply infrastructure for telecommunication equipment. A monitoring system supports the energy required for operating a telecommunication tower. In order to overcome the problem of monitoring solar power supplies in areas that are difficult to reach, an IoT platform is needed for remote monitoring and security of solar power supplies. The IoT platform has been designed to monitor battery voltage, charging current, battery discharge current and battery capacity status. The current and voltage sensor reading data during the charging and discharging process is used to predict the SoC of the battery as the basis for the operation of the relay disconnecting PV resources or loads. The battery management system consists of two cut off relay, which the cut-off relay #1 for charging and the cut-off relay #2 for discharging. The battery charge and discharge management system is expected to overcome the problem of a short VLRA battery lifetime.

articleTitle: Predicting Specific Heat Capacity of Nanofluids Using Artificial Neural Network for Al2O3 particle with EG/Water based solution
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This research presents comprehensive investigation of an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model for predicting specific heat capacity (SHC) of nanofluids. Study incorporates hyperparameter tuning to optimize the model's performance and accuracy. Dataset of 252 samples utilized comprises nanofluids consisting of aluminium nitride (Al2N3) nanoparticles suspended in water and ethylene glycol (EG) solution, with experimental SHC measurements recorded at different volume fractions and temperatures ranging from 296K to 336K. Additional input parameters, such as volume fractions, SHC of nanoparticles, and SHC of base fluids, are also included in dataset. The ANN model's performance is rigorously evaluated using various metrics, including Mean Squared Error and Mean Absolute Error. Remarkably, the ANN achieved an impressive accuracy of 94.44% for testing dataset and 98.57% for the training dataset, with absolute percentage errors of 5.562 and 1.433, respectively. These remarkably low errors validate the model's accuracy and reliability in predicting SHC for nanofluids. Further validation of the ANN model's performance is conducted by comparing its predicted SHC values with experimental data for various nanofluids, including nanoparticle Al2O3 dispersed in Ethylene Glycol (EG) and water base fluids. Results demonstrate a remarkable alignment between the ANN model's predictions and the experimentally derived SHC values, solidifying the model's accuracy and robustness. Research findings highlight the effectiveness of the ANN model in accurately predicting SHC for a diverse range of nanofluids. The successful hyperparameter tuning process further enhances the model's applicability in nanofluid research and underscores its potential for practical applications in heat transfer and energy systems involving nanofluids.

articleTitle: Unveiling Insights: An In-Depth Analysis and Exploratory Study of Crowdfunding Data Using Kickstarter as a Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Crowdfunding, facilitated by platforms like Kickstarter, has revolutionized fundraising by enabling individuals to gather financial support from a broad audience through online channels. Kickstarter specifically caters to creators and fundraisers seeking backing for various creative projects, including movies, music, games, and technology products. Fundraisers create campaign pages, setting specific funding goals and timelines. Supporters can contribute monetary donations towards these projects and, in return, receive rewards corresponding to their contribution level. In this study, exploratory data analysis was employed to gain descriptive insights into crowdfunding data from Kickstarter. This data analysis technique allowed for a comprehensive examination of the characteristics of the crowdfunding campaigns on the platform. Exploratory data analysis in the context of crowdfunding encompasses studying contributor profiles, identifying the most successful campaign types, and exploring other factors that can impact the success of a campaign. we identified several influential factors that significantly impact the success of a crowdfunding campaign, such as launch time, category, duration, and funding goals of crowdfunding campaign. The results from this study can be used to get better results from the decision-making and modelling process.

articleTitle: The Effects of Stopwords, Stemming, and Lemmatization on Pre-trained Language Models for Text Classification: A Technical Study
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Pre-trained models such as BERT and other models, including their variants, have different approaches to the embedding process and the use of vocabulary files. Therefore, the use of preprocessing on the data will affect how the input vector is formed. The lack of studies studying the effect of preprocessing on pre-trained models in natural language processing tasks such as text classification is an opportunity for more research. This study aims to seize this opportunity by conducting experiments on fine-tuning eight different pre-trained models for text classification tasks to investigate the effect of preprocessing techniques on a wider variety of pre-trained models. The combination of these preprocessing techniques was applied to see their impact on classification performance. Each model was also studied for its performance in the defined configuration. As a result, the use of preprocessing techniques such as stopword removal, stemming, and lemmatization does not significantly improve the performance of the classification model. The results also indicate that the use of stemming tends to decrease performance. By obtaining this information, it becomes clearer whether the use of such preprocessing techniques is still required when developing text classification applications in the world of pre-trained models.

articleTitle: Accurate Density Prediction of Nanofluids using an Optimized Artificial Neural Network for Enhanced Heat Transfer and Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This research presents an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model for accurate density prediction of nanofluids, showcasing its potential applications in heat transfer and energy systems. The ANN model's performance is rigorously evaluated, and the impact of hyperparameter tuning is thoroughly analysed. The results demonstrate the model's remarkable accuracy, achieving 99.60% for the testing dataset and 99.51% for the training dataset. The absolute percentage error (APE) values are remarkably low, validating the model's precision in predicting density. Comparative analysis between the ANN's predictions and experimental data further confirms its reliability. Hyperparameter tuning significantly enhances the model's accuracy and generalization capabilities. The developed ANN model opens new possibilities for advancing nanofluid research and optimizing heat transfer technologies. Its versatility and potential for broader applications in nanofluid behaviours make it a valuable tool for sustainable engineering practices.

articleTitle: Design of COIN Wifi Based on Microcontroller Embedded System NodeMCU
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This research presents the concept of Coin WiFi, which combines the convenience of wireless connectivity with the functionality of coin-operated systems. Coin WiFi operates as a WiFi hotspot, utilizing radio waves to enable fast and secure data transmission. Similar to inserting a coin into a public telephone to activate its usage, Coin WiFi machines can be connected to various internet service providers. The design of Coin WiFi focuses on user-friendliness, ensuring that even nontechnical individuals can easily operate it. This ease of use is achieved through the integration of a NodeMCU microcontroller, which is embedded within the Coin WiFi machine. The practicality and accessibility of Coin WiFi make it a suitable solution for providing wireless internet access to a wide range of users.

articleTitle: Jammer Detection on Embedded Android Implementation: Blue Bird Group Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: As one of the largest transportation companies in Indonesia. Blue Bird Group know that keeping our driver competition healthy is one of the biggest concerns of our engineering team. The malicious behaviour of one driver can affect other drivers’ performance. The presence of the Internet of Things (IoT) in Blue Bird Group’s fleet can provide a predictive detection of such behaviour so that the operation team can act accordingly. This paper provides an overview of the Blue Bird Group’s implementation of jammer detection to minimize the usage of jamming devices and build trust among our drivers. In each of our fleets, there is an IoT device embedded to help our driver receive orders and the company track its fleet. The idea is to embed an artificial intelligence model on the IoT device and use Android API to provide information for the artificial intelligence model to process. Blue Bird Group also build a web-based control centre that provides information on the malicious driver’s behaviour. The first model has 94.18% accuracy and 11% loss, and the second model has 100% accuracy and 0% loss.

articleTitle: Analysis of Social Media Data Using Contextual Embedding Leverage Models with Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This research proposes a model approach that uses leverage contextual embedding with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) in the context of sentiment analysis. The use of contextual embedding leverage aims to get a more contextual representation of words by using BERT. The results obtained from this study are a combination of batch size and epoch parameters with parameter values including batch values of 36, epoch values of 30 get an accuracy of 0.84, batch size values of 64, epoch values of 60 get an accuracy of 0.89, batch size values of 128, epoch values of 80 get an accuracy of 0.92 and batch size value of 256, epoch value of 100 obtains an accuracy of 0.94. so that the combination of CNN parameters and the use of contextual embedding leverage affects accuracy. This research is expected to provide an understanding of semantics in the context of sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: New Approach Monitoring System with ESP32 and MQTT for the Best Position of the Floating Net Cage
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: One of the most popular fish-raising techniques is floating net cages (KJA). In order to maintain the sustainability of the local fish population, the KJA must maintain a suitable placement position and keep an eye on the state of the water. Because of this, it is essential to design a system that will accommodate the circumstances at the KJA location. Hence, we selected ESP32 and MQTT to build a DO, pH, and temperature sensor-based water quality monitoring system. IoT and MQTT Protocol Implementation for Monitoring System represents the proposed work. The outcomes indicate a system that can be verified whenever needed and delivers recommendations on where to position the KJA by using an LED indicator on the dashboard system.

articleTitle: Clustering Digital Transformation of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) Using Fuzzy K-means Method
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Digital transformation of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) is an effort to advance the competitiveness and productivity of SMEs through grouping based on specific criteria. One of the clustering techniques that can be used is Fuzzy K-means. This method allows for a more flexible grouping of SMEs, bearing in mind that each SME can have different relationships in each group. This study aims to apply the Fuzzy K-means method in an information system for SME clustering based on the variables Type of SME product, Dynamic Capabilities, Workforce Transformation, and SME Performance. The results of this study indicate that there are three groups of SMEs, namely large, medium and small enterprises. This research can provide critical information for the government and SME support institutions as a decision support system in providing more targeted assistance and support for each SME group. In addition, the results of this study can also help SMEs to increase their competitiveness and productivity through increasing access to markets, technology, and capital following the characteristics of the SME group.

articleTitle: Enhancing Diabetic Retinopathy Classification for Small Sample Training Data Through Supervised Feature Attention: Transfer and Multitask Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: This study introduces a framework aimed at bolstering the effectiveness of deep learning models in image classification tasks, with a specialized focus on diabetic retinopathy detection. The proposed strategy employs transfer and multitask learning methods for the consistent extraction of insights and refinement of pre-established models. The capability of multitask learning to simultaneously acquire knowledge from numerous related tasks, leveraging shared information and inter-dependencies, leads to considerable performance boosts. Integrated into this process is the feature guideline learning task, which empowers the model to have an attention to abnormal areas. This task is initially trained on a small collection of labeled images to develop a custom pre-trained model, which later forms the basis for subsequent classification tasks. The effectiveness of this proposed approach is validated through tests on various data sets. It has been proven that our method contributes considerable advancements in image classification performance. This research offers valuable perspectives on the detection and classification of diabetic retinopathy, providing solutions to problems originating from limited data, and shows promising potential for improving patient care.

articleTitle: Pre-Processing Of Resize And Region Of Interest (ROI) To Improve The Accuracy Of Batik Detection Based On VGG-16
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: The patterns and designs used in batik are a traditional textile art form from Indonesia. With the increasing popularity of computer vision applications, the interest in automatic detection and recognition of batik patterns is increasing. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) show very good performance in detecting objects. The problem addressed in this study is the variation in image sizes, which affects accuracy. The selection of pre-processing techniques will impact the accuracy of the results. For this reason, it is important in this study to compare tests on data that has been processed using resize and Region of Interest (ROI). This study aims to determine the impact of two pre-processing techniques, resize and ROI, on the accuracy of batik pattern recognition using the Visual Geometry Group (VGG)-16 model. The dataset consisted of 1,445 images, with 1,301 images used for training and 144 images used for testing. The classes used were Kawung, Parang, Satriomanah, Sawat, Sementrante, Sidomukti, Tambal, and Truntum. The experimental results demonstrate that the choice of pre-processing techniques significantly affects the accuracy of batik pattern detection. Resizing provides an efficient computational solution, while ROI achieves a detection accuracy of 0.96, which is superior to Resize's accuracy of 0.89. This study highlights the importance of preprocessing techniques in detecting batik patterns using the VGG-16 model. Resizing and ROI have advantages and disadvantages, ROI techniques generally result in higher accuracy.

articleTitle: Prototype Design of an Electricity Power Monitoring System Based on Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Informatics (EECSI)
abstract: Electrical energy is essential to meeting all human demands, particularly those of the domestic and industrial nature.
